editorial:
Steven Seagal plays an ex-cop drowning in gambling debt, and when a shadowy figure offers to wipe the slate clean in exchange for taking out the city's worst gangsters, you know things are about to get messy. The setup is classic Seagal territory: a flawed hero, a dark deal, and plenty of bad guys who need punching. The movie leans into its gritty crime vibe, with dimly lit streets and tense confrontations that keep you watching even when the plot gets a little predictable. Seagal brings his usual calm, tough-guy energy, and the supporting cast helps sell the world of underground crime and moral gray areas. It's not high art, but it delivers exactly what you'd expect from a late-era Seagal action flick.

Action scenes are the main draw here, with hand-to-hand fights and shootouts that move at a steady clip. The pacing stays brisk, though some dialogue scenes drag a bit. Pros include solid fight choreography and a moody atmosphere; cons are a thin script and a few wooden performances. If you're a Seagal fan or just want a no-frills action thriller, this is a fun weekend watch. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final act, Seagal's character realizes the mysterious man who hired him has been manipulating events all along, using him to eliminate rivals and consolidate power. After a brutal showdown, Seagal turns the tables, refusing to be a pawn. He confronts the mastermind, delivers justice, and walks away free of his debts but forever changed. The twist reveals the man was never truly helping him—he was just another gangster playing a longer game.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves action thrillers and Steven Seagal movies.
